findings.title: A warning within a finite audible interval
findings.claim: The focus tongue, warning, and addressed people meet 19:98's destroyed generations whom no one can sense or hear, down to the faintest sound. The contact makes the facilitated proclamation a present, transmissible voice set against the possible disappearance of a people's own audible trace.
findings.mechanism: The focus lisānaka, tundhira, and qawman carry embodied speech, warning, and a collective audience; the next verse supplies annihilation, sensory failure, hearing, and the lower acoustic limit of rukz. Their adjacency changes the tongue from a convenience alone into speech heard within a finite interval.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the warning's present audibility against the passage's immediately following image of vanished voices.
findings.containment: The next verse may illustrate destruction without contrasting human silence and revelatory transmission. No claim is made that the warning preserves a people's voice or guarantees its response.

epistemic.reason: The exact context coordinates and focus returns match; the relation between audible warning and finite interval remains an attributed inference.

findings.title: A protective warning resisted at the mouth
findings.claim: The focus places a warning through lisānaka before a self-guarding audience and a qawm called luddan; the l-d-d side-mouth specialization supplies an oral-dose image, while 19:86's coercive driving adds pressure. This contact permits an exploratory reading of the warning as a protective dose pressed toward resistant hearers.
findings.mechanism: The focus lisan, muttaqin, tundhira, and luddan are the carriers; the independent trigger is the side-mouth medicine specialization within l-d-d, joined to the separate driving scene in 19:86. The word-level image of dosing contacts the protective purpose of warning and the contextual pressure of being driven.
findings.reader_payoff: A difficult audience can be pictured as resisting a warning intended to protect, so the speech's urgency is felt without changing the adjective's ordinary sense.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed material analogy, not a lexical translation of qawman luddan and not a claim that the messenger literally forces a dose on anyone. The focus audience retains its ordinary contentiousness reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT coordinates and resolved side-mouth facet fit the supplied focus; the multi-step dose analogy remains unusually inferential and unbound.

findings.title: Good news against covering
findings.claim: The focus's ordinary glad-tidings verb and language medium meet the skin-surface branch of b-sh-r and 19:77's covered, manifest signs. The contact permits a surface analogy: good-news speech can bring a sign and its joy-bearing effect back into shared perceptibility.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are tubashshira through lisānaka and the supplied surface and glad-tidings branches; the independent trigger is 19:77's covering of manifest signs. Their contact reverses the image of covering with speech that exposes an affectively visible event.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the glad-tidings act as making something visible and shareable against the earlier image of covering.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory cross-domain analogy. Tubashshira retains its ordinary Form II glad-tidings sense; the verse does not say that disbelief literally covers skin or that proclamation reverses every act of disbelief.

epistemic.reason: The source coordinates and roots match, but the surface reversal is an unusual HFT inference and the contextual lexicon branches are unresolved.

findings.title: A root-level path resonance in the added overlay
findings.claim: The focus qawman is carried as an ordinary human collective, and its q-w-m root meets the explicit al-sirat al-mustaqim request in the added 1:6 overlay. With luddan naming resistance in the focus, this independent straight-path trigger adds a limited path-oriented resonance to the warned group.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus qawman; the external trigger is mustaqim in 1:6, whose supplied root occurrence is q-w-m. Their same-root contact activates uprightness as an overlay branch and lets the contentious group be heard against a requested straight course.
findings.reader_payoff: The added verse makes a directional contrast perceptible: the warning's contentious addressee can be heard alongside a request for an upright path.
findings.containment: The overlay does not translate qawm as path or say that 1:6 directly explains 19:97. The native group reading and its contentiousness remain intact; this is a small same-root resonance supplied only by 1:6.

epistemic.reason: The inline surfaces supply the focus carrier and external q-w-m trigger, but the interpretive change rests on a root-level resonance rather than an explicit cross-ayah statement.
